lede: The biggest thing to watch this week is Tuesday's CommonSpirit Health presentation to the Telluride Hospital District board — a single-item work session with no packet posted yet, on a potential partnership that could reshape how this valley gets its healthcare. Alongside that, the Housing Authority Subcommittee takes up a real policy knot around subpar bedrooms in mitigation units, and the county's housing code working group meets again to push forward Land Use Code changes meant to speed up affordable housing. On the lighter side, the Imogene Pass Run goes Saturday and the week opens with The Meditations at the Sheridan.

notable.stake: CommonSpirit partnership terms for the hospital district remain undisclosed to the public.
Policy decisions on subpar bedrooms in mitigation units could affect housing stock rules.
Code changes could remove Land Use barriers slowing affordable housing in unincorporated county.
Potential demolition of Town-owned Rebekah Hall gets a public work session before HARC.
Two public hearings on land subdivision and a PUD — residents may testify.
